name: Relative Strength Index (RSI)
description: RSI measures the speed and magnitude of price changes on a scale of 0-100. It compares average gains to average losses over a lookback period to assess overbought and oversold conditions. Default period is 14 bars. RSI is most reliable in ranging markets and must be interpreted differently during strong trends.

signals.interpretation: Potential end of oversold condition; bullish reversal signal when confirmed by price action or structure
Potential end of overbought condition; bearish reversal signal when confirmed by price action or structure
Overbought in ranging market; in strong uptrend this is normal and does not signal reversal alone
Oversold in ranging market; in strong downtrend this is normal and does not signal reversal alone

signals.condition: Regular bullish divergence: price makes lower low, RSI makes higher low
signals.interpretation: Bearish momentum is weakening; potential bullish reversal — high-probability signal especially at key support

signals.condition: Regular bearish divergence: price makes higher high, RSI makes lower high
signals.interpretation: Bullish momentum is weakening; potential bearish reversal — high-probability signal especially at key resistance

signals.condition: Hidden bullish divergence: price makes higher low, RSI makes lower low
signals.interpretation: Trend continuation signal in uptrend; pullback is likely over, trend likely to resume upward

signals.condition: Hidden bearish divergence: price makes lower high, RSI makes higher high
signals.interpretation: Trend continuation signal in downtrend; retracement is likely over, trend likely to resume downward
Strong uptrend regime; RSI does not reach oversold; pullbacks to 40-50 are buy zones not sell zones
Strong downtrend regime; RSI does not reach overbought; bounces to 50-60 are sell zones not buy zones
Bullish momentum shift; price is gaining upward momentum on average
Bearish momentum shift; price is losing upward momentum on average

rules.rule: Never use RSI overbought/oversold thresholds as standalone entry signals. Always require confirmation from price structure, support/resistance, or candlestick patterns.
rules.rationale: RSI can remain overbought or oversold for extended periods in trending markets, leading to premature entries against the trend.

rules.rule: Adjust RSI interpretation based on trend regime. In a strong uptrend, treat 40-50 as oversold and 70-80 as overbought. In a strong downtrend, treat 50-60 as overbought and 20-30 as oversold.
rules.rationale: Fixed thresholds fail in trending markets. RSI is biased by trend direction and must be recalibrated to the current regime.

rules.rule: Prioritize regular divergence signals at key structural levels (swing highs/lows, S/R zones, Fibonacci levels). Divergence without a structural confluence is lower probability.
rules.rationale: Divergence signals the weakening of momentum but price needs a reason (structure) to actually reverse. Confluence increases probability significantly.

rules.rule: Use hidden divergence for trend-following entries during pullbacks. Hidden bullish divergence on a pullback in an uptrend is a high-probability continuation signal.
rules.rationale: Hidden divergence aligns with the dominant trend, making it statistically more reliable than counter-trend regular divergence.

rules.rule: The RSI 50 level acts as a bull/bear line. Price holding above 50 on pullbacks favors bulls; price failing to reclaim 50 on bounces favors bears.
rules.rationale: RSI 50 represents equilibrium between average gains and losses. Sustained bias above or below 50 reflects trend direction.

rules.rule: Do not trade RSI divergence against a strong trend without higher-timeframe confirmation of a reversal. Wait for the higher timeframe to show a topping or bottoming pattern.
rules.rationale: Counter-trend trades carry higher risk. Higher-timeframe alignment dramatically improves reward-to-risk.

rules.rule: Use multiple timeframe RSI analysis. Daily RSI gives trend bias; 4H RSI provides entry context; 1H RSI gives precise entry timing.
rules.rationale: Single-timeframe RSI analysis misses the broader context and leads to fighting the dominant trend.

agent_use: Use RSI to assess momentum context and divergence. First determine trend regime (ranging vs trending) by checking price structure and EMA alignment. Apply fixed 30/70 thresholds only in ranging markets. In trends, shift thresholds to 40/80 (uptrend) or 20/60 (downtrend). Flag regular divergence at structural confluence as potential reversal warnings. Flag hidden divergence during pullbacks as continuation entries. Always combine RSI signal with at least one structural confirmation before generating a trade signal. Report RSI value, regime, any active divergence type, and the 50-line bias in analysis output.
